title: Inquest to review emergency room police shooting
article: As revellers gathered to celebrate the dawn of the year 2000, Henry Masuka walked into the emergency room of a downtown Toronto hospital with his sick infant son.
Forty-six minutes later, the 26-year-old father of four was pronounced dead, shot by police at the stroke of midnight.
Today, a coroner's inquest will begin reviewing the actions of Mr. Masuka, the hospital staff and police -- and ultimately make recommendations to prevent similar deaths in the future.

Although almost 16 months have passed, the Masuka family is still waiting for answers and hopes the inquest will provide them, their lawyer, Peter Rosenthal, said yesterday. The hearing is expected to last two weeks and hear from 25 witnesses.
The family requested an inquest into the shooting of Mr. Masuka, the family's sole breadwinner.

Witnesses told police the young father became angry when staff at St. Michael's Hospital told him he would have to wait 45 minutes before a pediatrician could see his three-month-old asthmatic son who was having trouble breathing. He was advised to go to the Hospital for Sick Children.
Instead, he grabbed a doctor around the throat and pointed what looked like a .45-calibre gun at his back and neck.

After he refused repeated requests to put down his weapon, two members of the Toronto Police emergency task force fired five shots at close range, three of them hitting Mr. Masuka. The weapon turned out to be an unloaded pellet gun.
The province's Special Investigations Unit cleared the officers of any criminal wrongdoing.

In announcing his decision, Peter Tinsley, the unit's director, said that Mr. Masuka taunted police with statements such as "Take me out" and "This will be over by midnight." Mr. Tinsley said the shooting was "legally justified" because police believed the doctor's life was in danger.
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates incidents in which members of the public are seriously injured, sexually assaulted or killed by police.
Mr. Rosenthal said the family believes the whole incident was very strange because Mr. Masuka had no history of mental problems or bizarre behaviour.
